item.title: Extracting Certificates from a PFX
item.description:
OpenSSL seperating a PFX into Public and Private Key Files

Using OpenSSL we can extract the private key, and the certificate into independent file’s, which is required for most networking devices, and linux services.

You will need to install the OpenSSL, package, either on your system.

Export the private key from the PFX file

We begin, by passing in the PFX and requesting the Private key to be placed into its own file. This process will require that you provide the password which is used to protect the PFX file, and also a new password to protect the new private key file (this is not optional).

item.title: Installing the Latest OpenSSL release
item.description:
Installing the Latest OpenSSL release on Ubuntu

Being over 25 years old, OpenSSL can be found on just about any system you work with today; but this does not imply that the version installed is current (or even close).

During its life, there have been many instances where OpenSSL has been in the news, where some new vulnerability has being discovered, and quickly after, patched.
